=== proposal.md
## Problem

The operator can't use the factory's own records to tell whether the factory is doing its job.

The factory is an AI pipeline. A written request becomes a ticket. AI roles (triage, a spec writer, an implementer, reviewers) each do one job on it in a "run", and the result is merged code. The factory keeps every ticket, run and decision in its store: a folder of files on a git branch of its own.

The north star, `docs/north-star.md`, is the page that says what the factory is for. The operator's approved plan for it (T-0055) names five numbers to watch every two weeks:
- changes merged into the product;
- escapes, meaning merged changes that later needed a fix or a revert;
- operator decisions and interventions per change;
- tokens and wall time per change;
- lead time from request to merge.

`factory stats`, the factory's read-only report on its store, counts what each role catches and costs. It counts none of those five numbers. The operator counted them once by hand, for 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-19. That count can't be repeated cheaply or checked.

Three things are missing from the store, so no report can compute the numbers:
- **Escapes aren't recorded anywhere.** Whether a merged change later needed a fix lives only in the operator's memory and in issue trackers. Some of those trackers are private.
- **Most runs have no cost record.** A run started by the newer driver, `factory drive`, records the tokens and dollars its AI process used. A run started by the Workflow scripts records nothing. The Workflow scripts are the original way of running the factory, inside a Claude Code session, and they start most runs. From 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-14, 23 of 26 triage runs and 64 of 66 implementer runs had no cost record.
- **Nothing says whose merges count as product work.** The factory runs on two repositories. Each has its own configuration and store, together called an "instance". One is a port of the Nanobot chat bot, which is product work. The other is the factory's own code. The operator decided that the factory's changes to itself are "factory work". They are reported on a line of their own and never counted as product changes.

Until these exist, no later factory ticket can say which number it moves, and the review every two weeks has to be counted by hand.

## Evidence

All commands ran from `~/dev/spec-factory` on `main` at `1321c17`, each through the briefing's wrapper with a throwaway HOME. T-0058.1 merged after the briefing was composed. It changes no file this spec touches, apart from README lines this spec doesn't edit.

Capabilities opened: `openspec/specs/factory-stats/spec.md`, `openspec/specs/build-dispatch/spec.md`, `openspec/specs/harness-docs/spec.md` and `openspec/specs/live-store-guard/spec.md` (all given in the input), and `openspec/specs/harness-code/spec.md`.

- **The request's cost figures reproduce.**
  - `bin/factory stats --store <this store> --store <Nanobot store> --since 2026-10-08 --until 2026-10-14` prints in section D `| triage | opus | 26 | … | record 3, transcript 0, none 23 |` and `| implementer | opus | 66 | … | record 2, transcript 0, none 64 |`, as the request says.
  - The same command with `--transcripts /Users/dphang/.claude/projects` prints `none 0` on all eight rows, in 13.7 s. For example, the implementer row reads `record 2, transcript 64, none 0`.
  - So every run without a cost record has a Claude Code transcript, and the existing matching rule finds it.
- **Only driver runs have a record.** I counted `runs/*/meta.yaml` by start date in both stores. Every run with a `reply.json` (a `factory drive` run) has a `claude:` cost record, and no run without one does. Spec-factory's 211 runs from 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-13 have none. Its runs from 2026-10-14 on are drive runs, and all have one.
- **Root cause in the code.**
  - `run finish` records a cost only from `--reply FILE` (`factory/cli.py:340-341`), reading the reply in `_claude_record` (`factory/cli.py:366-376`).
  - Only `factory drive` passes `--reply` (`factory/drive.py:228`, `:235`).
  - The Workflow scripts call `run finish ${runId}` with no reply (`factory/workflows/build.js:122`, `:134`; `factory/workflows/intake.js:126`, `:131`). The Workflow tool's `agent()` gives a script the agent's final text, or the object when a schema is given. The scripts use nothing else from it (`build.js:141`, `intake.js:137`: `typeof out === 'string' ? out.trim() : ''`).
  - I found no documentation of a usage or cost field on `agent()`'s result (web search, 2026-10-22). This is not verified either way.
  - Drive's stop path also finishes a run with no reply (`factory/drive.py:577`).
- **The transcript is complete by the time the run finishes.** I checked 6 Nanobot Workflow runs on 2026-10-14 and 31 spec-factory Workflow runs on 2026-10-13 with a prototype script in my scratch directory (`lastts.py`). For each run, the last record of the transcript the existing rule finds is 5 to 17 seconds before the run's recorded `finished`. None is later. Workflow agents' transcripts sit at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/subagents/workflows/wf_<id>/agent-<id>.jsonl`.
- **Where Claude Code keeps transcripts.**
  - Claude Code's settings page says that with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set, "Claude Code then stores your settings, session history, and plugins there instead" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings, fetched 2026-10-22).
  - Listing all 8,768 `*.jsonl` files under `~/.claude/projects` takes 0.2 s. 24 of them were modified on 2026-10-22.
- **Transcripts hold tokens but no dollars**, as README already says (`README.md:977-983`). A record taken from a transcript can hold tokens only.
- **No scorecard, escape or intervention code exists.** On `1321c17`, `bin/factory stats --scorecard …`, `bin/factory escape add …` and `bin/factory intervention add …` each exit 2 with argparse's usage error. The outputs are captured under `verification.md`.
- **The hand-counted baseline's method** is in `requests/T-0055.md` on the store branch, commit `02e403f`.
  - It defines a change as a parent ticket closed in the window with at least one `merge.done`.
  - CLI decisions are `approval.recorded` plus `human.resolved` events.
  - A hand transition is a `ticket.transition` by the operator that matches neither.
  - Lead time runs to the parent's last `merge.done`.
  - The event log has every event these definitions need. This store has 64 `merge.done`, 605 `ticket.transition`, 58 `approval.recorded` and 75 `human.resolved` events.
  - A transition's actor is `workflow`, `merge`, `parent-check` or `ready-implementers` when the harness made it, and a login name when a person did. `factory drive` also writes `workflow` (`factory/drive.py:168`).
- **A person's transition can be paired with its CLI decision.**
  - `approve-spec` writes `approval.recorded` and its `ticket.transition` in the same call (`factory/human.py:156-159`).
  - In this store, 58 of a person's transitions have a decision on the same ticket within 2 seconds, and 7 have none. In the Nanobot store the figures are 33 and 19.
- **A spec amendment and a gate edit each log one `spec.added` whose source isn't a run id** (`gate edit <file>` or `amend <file>`; `factory/common.py:38`). An amendment also logs `spec.amended`, so counting `spec.added` alone counts each one once.
- **A parent's lead time can only start at its `ticket.created` event.** The store holds no request or issue date: `tickets/T-0054.yaml` has only `created`, `request` and `source`.
- **I prototyped the scorecard rules.**
  - A throwaway Python script in my scratch directory (`proto.py`) implements Proposed change part C. Over the fixture of the first factory-stats scenario, it prints exactly the THEN lines of two scenarios: "The scorecard gives each instance's measures for the window and the window before, and writes nothing" and "The scorecard takes a run's tokens from its transcript when the run has no cost record". I also counted those figures by hand.
  - I also ran it over both live stores for 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-19. For the Nanobot store's first window it prints a lead-time median of 21.9 h and a wall-time median of 1.2 h. The baseline's hand count is 21.8 h and 70 min, for a window one day longer. The windows differ, so this is a plausibility check, not a reproduction.
- **README draft.** I applied Proposed change part E to a copy of `README.md`.
  - It adds 36 lines and removes 8, taking README from 1,176 to 1,204 lines.
  - It passes this change's documents scenario.
  - It still passes the current-truth harness-docs scenarios "Each Built entry is a short pointer, and each mechanism's detail has one home", "The documents record factory stats" and "README no longer calls run features untried".
  - It has no whitespace error.
- **README budget.** README has 1,176 lines on `1321c17`, and current truth caps it at 1,185. T-0055, which is `planned`, adds 8 lines and checks the 1,185 cap in its own spec.
- **Module pins.** The harness-code scenario "The human decisions live in factory/human.py" prints the exact list of `factory/human.py`'s top-level names. `factory/cli.py` has 880 lines and must stay under 900 (same requirement).
- **Tests that pin what changes.**
  - `tests/factory/test_drive.py:82` and `:177` assert that `claude` is `None` after a reply that isn't a JSON object.
  - `tests/factory/test_drive.py:167` asserts the reply record's exact keys.
  - No test pins the Workflow scripts' `run finish` command text or `factory/human.py`'s names (`grep -rn "run finish" tests/factory/*.py`).

## Root cause

- **Escapes:** nothing records them. No command or event exists.
- **Cost:** `run finish` takes a cost record only from a process reply (`factory/cli.py:340-341`), and only `factory/drive.py` produces one. Three kinds of run finish with no reply:
  - the Workflow scripts' runs (`factory/workflows/intake.js:131`, `build.js:134`);
  - both scripts' KILLED path;
  - drive's stopped runs (`factory/drive.py:577`).

  Their tokens stay only in Claude Code's transcript, which `factory stats` reads only when given `--transcripts`.
- **Scorecard:** `factory/stats.py` has only sections A to D, and no instance declares what its merges count as.

## Out of scope

- `factory stats` sections A to D, with or without `--transcripts`. Their code, columns and current-truth scenarios stay as they are.
- Back-filling cost records for runs that already ended. The scorecard and section D still read those runs' transcripts when given `--transcripts`.
- Dollars for a run whose record comes from a transcript. Transcripts hold no dollars, and no estimate is recorded.
- What the baseline counted but the store can't: merges made outside the factory, operator hours, decisions made only in chat, commands typed outside Claude Code, and the cost of the Workflow scripts' own clerk agent (the agent that runs each store command for a script).
- `docs/north-star.md`, `docs/design.md`, `docs/changelog.md`, `docs/prompts/`, `agents/` and every role prompt.
- The live-store fence's read-only list. The fence is the harness's refusal of unmarked store writes while a run is in flight. The two new commands are writes, so they stay fenced.
- The Nanobot instance's `instance.yaml`. It needs no change, because a missing setting means target changes.

## Open questions

1. **How should an intervention made outside the CLI be recorded?** The operator asked for options at this gate (Answer 1).

   The scorecard can already count three kinds of intervention from the store:
   - a `ticket transition` by a person that no approval or `resolve` made;
   - each spec version the operator wrote (gate edits and amendments);
   - each `decision add` line.

   Hand commits, runs stopped by hand, actions after a classifier refusal and decisions made in chat leave no event.

   - (a) **Recommended.** A new command, `factory intervention add --kind <word> [--ticket T-n] [--note "<line>"]`, writes one `intervention.recorded` event, and the scorecard counts it. The operator, or a runner session acting for the operator, runs it after each such action. It's cheap, explicit, and the same shape as `factory escape add`. Its weakness is that it counts only what someone remembers to record.
   - (b) Option (a), plus a count of the operator's non-merge commits on the integration branch that touch a protected path, such as the gate config or `.factory/`. This is more automatic. But deciding which commits are interventions is a judgment, as the baseline's last caveat says, and it means the report reads git, which it doesn't do today.
   - (c) No record. The scorecard counts only what the store already shows, and README says the rest isn't counted.

   This spec is written for (a). Five pieces depend on that choice:
   - Proposed change part B2;
   - the scenario "An intervention recorded outside the CLI is counted by the scorecard";
   - the `intervention_add` name in the modified harness-code scenario;
   - the README row **Intervene**;
   - the `intervene=` field of the documents scenario.

   Choosing (c) removes all five. Choosing (b) keeps them and needs one more part. The answer is standing: later tickets and runner sessions record interventions the way chosen here.
2. **May an escape's issue link be written to a store that's pushed to a public remote?** The request records `--issue <url>` and keeps the link out of the public review. But this repository is public and its store branch is on GitHub. A link to a private tracker becomes public when the operator pushes the store.
   - (a) **Recommended.** Record the link as given, as the request asks, and say in README that the store keeps it. When the link itself is private, the operator passes a reference that identifies nothing, such as a private tracker's ticket number.
   - (b) Record no link in the store. `--issue` is still required, but only a fixed-length hash of it is kept, so the operator can match a record to its issue and nobody else can.

   This spec is written for (a). Choosing (b) changes part B1 and the escape scenario's event check, not the scorecard. The answer is standing for every later record that carries a link.

## Decisions

**How the scorecard is asked for**
- The scorecard is opt-in. `factory stats --scorecard --since WHEN [--until WHEN] [--transcripts DIR]…` prints only the scorecard, so a review can paste the whole output. Without `--scorecard`, the output is byte for byte what it is today.
- The current window is `[--since, --until)`, and the previous window is the same length, just before it. `--until` defaults to now. `--scorecard` without `--since` is refused with exit 2.

**Which instance a store belongs to**
- Each instance declares its kind with an optional `target_is_factory: true|false` in its `instance.yaml` (Answer 1, standing).
  - Missing or false: the instance's merges are target changes.
  - Any other value: `stats --scorecard` refuses with exit 2.
- `factory stats` finds a store's instance in the nearest directory above the store that holds a `.factory/instance.yaml` whose `state_dir` resolves to that store. It names the store's table after that directory.
- A store with no such instance is named by its path, its heading says "no instance found", and its merges count as target changes.

**What each row counts**
- A change is a parent ticket (an id with no `.N`) whose last `ticket.transition` to `closed` falls in the window and that has at least one `merge.done`, for itself or a sub-ticket. This matches the baseline.
- An escape counts in the window in which its change closed, provided it was recorded before the report's end. A change with several escape records counts once. The row prints ticket ids, never links or notes (request part B).
- CLI decisions are the `approval.recorded` and `human.resolved` events in the window.
- Interventions are these events in the window:
  - a `ticket.transition` whose `by` isn't `workflow`, `merge`, `parent-check` or `ready-implementers`, with no `approval.recorded` or `human.resolved` event for the same ticket within 2 seconds;
  - a `spec.added` whose source isn't a run id;
  - a `decision.recorded` with `via: decision add`;
  - an `intervention.recorded` (open question 1).
- "Decisions and interventions per change" is their sum divided by the window's changes. It stands in for hours of operator attention, per T-0055's standing decision. Standing: a later ticket that adds a human command says whether it counts as a decision or an intervention.
- The row name stays T-0055's "Tokens and wall time per change", which settles triage's wording gap.
  - Its first line is the median, over the window's changes, of each change's summed run wall time, in hours.
  - Its sub-rows are the median tokens (context plus output) over the changes whose every run has tokens, the count of runs by token source, and the dollars on the records that carry them.
  - Dollars are reported but never estimated.
- A change's runs are every finished run of the parent and its sub-tickets, killed ones included, because killed runs took time and tokens. The baseline summed only `run.finished` events, so this figure runs slightly higher than a baseline-style count.
- A run's tokens come from its cost record. Failing that, with `--transcripts`, they come from the transcript that section D's rule finds, as section D does today.
- Lead time runs from the parent's `ticket.created` event to its last `merge.done`. The baseline started from the earliest of three dates: the request's date, the issue's creation and the ticket's creation. The store holds only the last, so for a request filed late this figure can be shorter than the baseline's.

**The token record**
- The cost root cause is fixed where the record is written. `run finish --transcripts DIR` (repeatable) records the tokens of the run's transcript when the run has no reply usage.
- Both Workflow scripts pass `--transcripts` on every `run finish`. `factory drive` passes it on all three of its `run finish` calls.
- The directory is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, or `$HOME/.claude/projects` when that variable is unset. Callers pass it explicitly; `run finish` never defaults it. That way a test with a throwaway HOME never reads the operator's transcripts.
- A transcript record goes under the run's existing `claude:` key as `{source: transcript, transcript: <path>, usage: {input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, output_tokens}, total_cost_usd: null}`.
  - Section D therefore counts it as a record, with no change to section D's code.
  - Section D's "USD from records" column then covers only the records that carry dollars, and README says so.
  - A reply record keeps its exact current shape (`tests/factory/test_drive.py:167`).
- `run finish` matches a transcript with the rule section D already uses (`factory/cost.py` `match_transcripts`), for that one store and run. There's no upper time bound, because the run is finishing. It opens only files modified at or after the run's `started`.

**The two new commands**
- `factory escape add <ticket> --issue <link> [--note "<line>"]` writes one `escape.recorded` event and nothing else.
  - It's refused with exit 2, writing nothing, for an unknown ticket, a sub-ticket id (the message names the parent), a ticket with no `merge.done` for itself or a sub-ticket, or an empty `--issue`.
  - The ticket doesn't need to be closed yet.
- Both new commands are writes. The fence's first requirement already refuses every command outside its read-only list while a run is in flight, unless the command carries the marker. So both are refused unmarked during a run, and live-store-guard doesn't change.
- `escape_add` and `intervention_add` go in `factory/human.py`, next to `decision_add`. The harness-code requirement that pins that module's names is modified to list them. Rejected: a new module, because the harness-code checks read only the five split modules and wouldn't cover it.

**Documents and build**
- README's line budget rises from 1,185 to 1,225 lines. This change adds at most 30 lines net; the draft adds 28. The operator approves the new figure at this gate.
- There is no changelog entry, because `docs/design.md` doesn't change. Precedent: T-0049.
- The change is built as two seams (design.md, "Size and seams").

## Risk

**Blast radius.** Harness code changes in five places:
- the stats report, which only gains new read-only output;
- `run finish`, which gains a new optional flag;
- both Workflow scripts, which gain one argument on every `run finish`;
- the driver, which gains the same argument on every `run finish`;
- two new commands.

**The riskiest piece is the scripts' `run finish` command.** A mistake there, such as an unescaped `${…}` inside the JavaScript template string, would fail every run finish and park every ticket as `harness-bug: run finish …`. The scenario "A run the intake script starts carries its transcript's tokens" runs the real intake script under node. Part D's suite test drives build.js the same way.

**Other effects.**
- A Workflow run whose transcript can't be found records no cost, as today. Nothing parks for it.
- `run finish` reads files under the operator's Claude Code directory, read-only. No scenario reads the real directory.
- The cost record's file path names the operator's home directory in the store. Run records already do this for worktrees.
- An escape's link is written to the store (open question 2).

**Build order.** Build this ticket after T-0055 closes. T-0055's own scenario checks that README is 1,185 lines or fewer. This change takes README past that, so if it merged first, T-0055 would fail its final check.

Protected paths: `factory/**`

## Operator steps

1. After the merge, add `target_is_factory: true` to this repository's `.factory/instance.yaml` (protected), with a one-line comment, and commit it on `main`. Leave the Nanobot instance's `instance.yaml` unchanged.
2. Upgrade the runtime and accept the revision in both instances as usual (README "Upgrading the runtime"). Before the next Workflow run, write fresh launch copies with `factory launch-script intake|build`. A launch copy written before the upgrade still calls `run finish` without `--transcripts`.
3. After the upgrade, check one real Workflow run and one real drive run with `grep -A2 '^claude:' <store>/runs/<run>/meta.yaml`. The Workflow run should show `source: transcript`, and the drive run should show `total_cost_usd`. The scenarios use stand-ins for Claude Code, so only this step confirms where Claude Code writes transcripts on this machine.
4. Optional: record the escapes the baseline review lists, with `FACTORY_DISPATCH=1 $RUNTIME/bin/factory escape add T-n --issue <link>` in each instance. Which ones to record is your call; the baseline marks some as "record only".

=== design.md
## Proposed change

**A. A token record for every run (build-dispatch).**

A1. `factory/cost.py`: add a function that returns a run's transcript record, or `None`. Its inputs are the transcript directories, a store path, a run id and the run's `started`.
- It walks `*.jsonl` at any depth under each directory, and opens only files whose modification time is at or after `started`.
- It applies `match_transcripts`' rule for that one store and run:
  - the first user message that isn't a relayed request must name `<P>/runs/<run>/`;
  - the transcript's first timestamp must be at or after `started`;
  - a candidate on the store's own path wins, else a single candidate is taken.
- It sums the four usage fields over the transcript, counting each message id once with its last record's usage, as `transcript_usage` does.
- The record is `{"source": "transcript", "transcript": <path>, "usage": {"input_tokens": …, "cache_read_input_tokens": …, "cache_creation_input_tokens": …, "output_tokens": …}, "total_cost_usd": None}`.
- `cost.py` keeps no import from the `factory` package (T-0046's decision).
- Reuse `match_transcripts`' helpers rather than copying them, for example by giving it an optional modification-time floor.

A2. `factory/cli.py` `run_finish` and its parser: add `--transcripts DIR` (`action="append"`, default `[]`).
- After the `--reply` handling, check whether the recorded `claude` value has a `usage` mapping. It has none when there's no `--reply`, or when the reply isn't a JSON object or has no `usage`.
- If it has none and the function in A1 finds a record, set `meta["claude"]` to that record.
- Otherwise nothing changes from today. A reply with usage is kept in its current shape, and an unusable reply with no transcript still records `claude: null`.
- Keep `cli.py` under 900 lines (current truth; it has 880). Parts A, B and C together may add at most 19 lines to it.

A3. `factory/workflows/intake.js` and `build.js`:
- Define once per script `const TRANSCRIPTS = '"${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects"'`. It's a plain string, so JavaScript doesn't interpolate it.
- Append ` --transcripts ${TRANSCRIPTS}` to every `run finish` clerk command: the normal one, and the KILLED one after a thrown agent call.
- Change nothing else in either script.

A4. `factory/drive.py`: pass `--transcripts <dir>` on its three `run finish` calls (`:228`, `:235`, `:577`).
- `<dir>` is `os.environ["CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"] + "/projects"` when that variable is set and non-empty, else `os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")`.
- It comes from the driver's own environment, which its role processes inherit.

**B. Records the scorecard counts (factory-stats).**

B1. `factory/human.py` `escape_add`, and its parser in `cli.py`: `factory escape add TICKET --issue TEXT [--note TEXT]`.
- Load the ticket. An unknown ticket exits 2.
- Refuse a sub-ticket id with `escape add: <id> is a sub-ticket; record the escape on its parent <parent>`.
- Read the log through `store.log_lines`. If no `merge.done` names the id or `<id>.N`, refuse with `escape add: <id> has no merge`.
- Refuse an empty `--issue`.
- Every refusal exits 2 and writes nothing.
- Otherwise write one event, `store.log_event(root, "escape.recorded", ticket=<id>, issue=<text>, by=_by())`, plus `note=` when given, and print `{"ok": true, "id": <id>, "issue": <text>}`.
- Add no other top-level name to `human.py`.

B2. (Open question 1, option (a).) `factory/human.py` `intervention_add`, and its parser: `factory intervention add --kind WORD [--ticket TICKET] [--note TEXT]`.
- `--kind` is required and must be non-empty.
- A given ticket must exist, in any state; otherwise exit 2.
- Write one `intervention.recorded` event with `kind` and `by`, plus `ticket` and `note` when given.
- Print `{"ok": true, "kind": …}`, plus `"id"` when a ticket was given.

Neither command joins the fence's read-only list.

**C. The scorecard (factory-stats).**
- `factory/stats.py` gains a scorecard report.
- `cli.py`'s `stats` parser gains `--scorecard` (`store_true`). When it's set, `stats_cmd` calls the scorecard instead of `report()`.
- Sections A to D and `report()` don't change.

C1. Refusals. Each exits 2 and prints nothing on stdout:
- `--scorecard` without `--since`: `factory stats: --scorecard needs --since`.
- An instance file whose `target_is_factory` is present and isn't a boolean: `factory stats: target_is_factory in <file> must be true or false`.

C2. Windows.
- `end` is `--until`, else now.
- The current window is `[since, end)`. The previous window is `[since - (end - since), since)`.
- A bound is printed as `YYYY-MM-DD` when it's midnight UTC, else as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` (UTC).

C3. For each `--store`, in the order given, find its instance (proposal, Decisions). Then count from the store's `runs/*/meta.yaml` and its log, read with `cost._log_records` as `report()` does. Each definition below applies per window:
- **changes:** as in Decisions. A sub-ticket is `<parent>.N`.
- **escapes:** changes with an `escape.recorded` event for the change id dated before `end`. Printed as `0`, or as `<n> (<ids sorted, ", "-separated>)`.
- **decisions D and interventions I:** as in Decisions. "Within 2 seconds" means the two events' timestamps differ by at most 2 s either way. Per change: `f"{(D + I) / n:.1f}"`, or `-` when n is 0.
- **a change's runs:** runs whose ticket is the change or `<change>.N`, at any date, whose status is set and isn't `running`.
- **a run's tokens:** the four fields of its `claude.usage` mapping, summed. Failing that, when `--transcripts` finds a transcript for it, that transcript's context plus output tokens. Finding uses `match_transcripts` over all `--store`s, as `report()` does. Failing both, the run has no tokens.
- **wall:** per change, the sum of its runs' `wall_s`. A missing value counts as 0.
- **lead:** per change that has a `ticket.created` event, the time from that event to the change's latest `merge.done`, for itself or a sub-ticket.
- **hours:** printed as `f"{seconds / 3600:.1f}"`.
- **median-and-range cell:** `<median> h (<min> to <max> h)`, using `statistics.median`, or `-` when there are no values.
- **tokens cell:** `<median> (<k> of <n>)`. k counts the changes whose every run has tokens, and the median is taken over those k changes and rounded down to a whole number. When k is 0, the cell is `- (0 of <n>)`.
